rationale: Kept: the geometry (five sensors at x = -0.02 to 0.02 m, y = 0.05 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg), sensor weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), kp = 3.0, base_speed = 1.5, line_loss = last_direction, and the full measurement request. The critique's main points were checked against the contract. (1) Sensor span: the critique is right that the centres span 0.04 m (about 1.6 tape widths), not 0.8. I accept the correction and will not claim the array is narrow. I keep the layout because no race data shows a coverage problem, and changing it now would confound the first telemetry. (2) Off-track limit: the critique is right that the 0.06 m floor governs for every allowed body width, so body_width is not a tuning lever; I stop describing it as one and keep 0.12 m. (3) base_speed is a duty fraction (75% PWM), not a ground speed. I accept this and keep 1.5 as a starting point, since the first race will measure completion_time and progress directly. (4) Derivative noise: accepted. Differentiating about 2% sensor noise at 100 Hz can add steering jitter, so I reduce kd from 0.3 to 0.15. (5) Integral term: accepted that ki = 0.1 with a +/-2 cap is nearly inert, so I lower it to 0.05 and keep it small only as a drift guard. (6) Turn authority: I partly reject this. At base 3071 PWM and maximum turn 6 (350 x 6 = 2100 PWM), the inner wheel command is 971 PWM, not zero or below, so there is no saturation at the chosen speed. I keep kp = 3.0 for now. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend with lower steering_oscillation than iteration 0 would have produced; slalom line loss and speed sufficiency remain unverified, and the telemetry should show which.
